segments.text: Queſt. 29th. What is the Law of God?
Anſ. God ſpake all theſe Words, Exod. xx. Deut. v. ſaying, I am the Lord thy God, which hath brought thee out of the Land of Egypt, out of the Houſe of Bondage.

I. COM. Thou ſhalt have no other Gods before me.
II. COM. Thou ſhalt not make unto thyſelf any graven Image, nor the Likeneſs of any Thing that is in Heaven above, or in the Earth beneath, or in the Water under the Earth. Thou ſhalt not bow down to them, nor ſerve them; for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, viſiting the Iniquity of the Fathers upon the Children, unto the third and fourth Generation of them that hate me, and ſhewing Mercy unto thouſands of them that love me, and keep my Commandments.
III. COM. Thou ſhalt not take the Name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltleſs, that taketh his Name in vain.
IV. COM. Remember the Sabbath Day, to keep it holy, ſix Days ſhalt thou labour, and do all thy Work, but the ſeventh Day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God: In it thou ſhalt do no Manner of Work, thou nor thy Son, nor thy Daughter, thy Man Servant, nor thy Maid Servant, nor thy Cattle, nor the Stranger that is within thy Gates. For in Six Days the Lord made Heaven and Earth, the Sea, and all that in them is, and reſted the ſeventh Day; wherefore the Lord bleſſed the Sabbath Day, and hallowed it.
V. COM. Honour thy Father and thy Mother, that thy Days may be long in the Land, which the Lord thy God giveth thee.
VI. COM. Thou ſhalt not kill.
VII. COM. Thou ſhalt not commit Adultery.
VIII. COM. Thou ſhalt not ſteal.
IX. COM. Thou ſhalt not bear falſe Witneſs againſt thy Neighbour.
X. COM. Thou ſhalt not covet thy Neighbour's Houſe, thou ſhalt not covet thy Neighbour's Wife, nor his Servant, nor his Maid, nor his Ox, nor his Aſs, nor any thing that is thy Neighbour's.
Queſt. 93. How are theſe ten Commands divided?

Anſ. Into two
Tables, the
firſt of which teaches us how we muſt behave towards God; the ſecond, what Duties we owe to our Neighbour.
Queſt. 94. What doth God enjoin in the firſt Command?

Anſw. That I, as ſincerely as I deſire the Salvation of my own Soul, avoid and flee from all Idolatry,
Sorcery,
Soothſaying, Superſtition,
Invocation of Saints, or any other Creatures, and learn
rightly to know the only true God: s truſt in him alone; with Humility t and Patience
ſubmit to Him,
expect all good Things from Him only;
love,
fear, and
glority Him with my whole Heart: So that I renounce
and forſake all Creatures, rather than
commit even the leaſt Thing, contrary to his Will.
Anſ. Idolatry is inſtead of, or beſides that one true God, who has manifeſted Himſelf in His Word, to contrive, or have any other Object in which Men place their Truſt.
